China's Consumer and Producer Inflation Edged Higher in August
China's consumer and factory-gate prices edged higher in August, fueled by energy-market jitters tied to renewed tensions in the Middle East.

The producer-price index climbed 3.8% in August from a year earlier, accelerating from July's 3.5% increase,  data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed Wednesday. The figure topped the median 3.7% increase projected by economists in a Wall Street Journal poll.

Factory-gate prices have risen for the sixth month in a row, driven by soaring oil costs stemming from the Middle East conflict. The trend marks a stark reversal from an extended, three-plus-year slump that began in late 2022.
On a monthly basis, producer prices rose 0.4% in August, improving from July's 0.7% decline, shrugging off the impact from adverse weather conditions that disrupted factory activities nationwide.
Meanwhile, China's consumer price rose 0.8% from a year earlier, faster than July's 0.5% growth and in line with the 0.8% increase expected by economists surveyed in the WSJ poll.
Core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, rose 1.0% in August from a year earlier, inching up from a 0.9% gain in the previous month.
